input_user_request: Plan a 21-day trip for a group of 7 travellers (22 Sep – 15 Oct 2023) covering South Korea (Busan, Seoul) and Japan (Hiroshima/Miyajima, Osaka, Kyoto, Sapporo, Tokyo). The group voted every candidate activity 1–5 and only the highest-scoring items should survive. The absolute anchor is a 2-day pass to Universal Studios Japan in Osaka, which the whole group rated 5/5. Travel inside Japan must be routed on a JR Pass wherever possible. Base each city block on a pre-booked Airbnb, and respect intercity flights and the Korea-to-Japan hop. Keep culture-heavy days balanced against the gaming/anime days the younger travellers voted for.

constraints.must_visit_location: Universal Studios Japan (Osaka) — 2-day pass, unanimous 5/5 vote
specific_hard_bounds: Universal Studios Japan 2-day pass booked for 04–05 Oct 2023, park entry at 07:30 both days (confirmation 4854221679)
Samurai Sword Experience in Kyoto is a fixed timed slot: 08 Oct 2023 at 13:00 (booking #S452074)
Gyeongbokgung Palace is closed every Tuesday; Changdeokgung Palace is closed every Monday — both must fall on the same non-Mon/non-Tue day if grouped
Busan Blue Line Park sky capsule requires online reservation opening exactly 2 weeks before the date of use and caps each booking at 4 passengers, so a party of 7 must be split into two bookings
Flight Incheon (ICN) → Fukuoka (FUK) departs 07:50 on 01 Oct 2023; airport transfer must start before 05:30
Flight Narita (NRT) → Busan (PUS) departs 11:15 on 24 Sep 2023, arriving 13:40 — first Korean activity cannot start before 15:00
Flight Narita (NRT) → Sapporo New Chitose (CTS) departs 08:25 on 10 Oct 2023
Miyajima is reachable only by ferry from Miyajimaguchi station; last usable return ferry that evening was 21:30
Ghibli Museum (Tokyo) requires advance timed-entry tickets bought a month ahead and is closed Tuesdays — it scored 29/35 in the vote but could not be secured
JR Pass does not cover Nozomi/Mizuho shinkansen or the Narita Express, so those legs must be re-routed or paid separately
Busan Airbnb check-in is 17:00 and check-out 13:00; early entry is billed per hour and must be pre-announced

expected_output_ground_truth: Day 1 (24 Sep, Busan): land PUS 13:40 → Haeundae Beach 15:00 → Airbnb check-in 17:00. Day 2 (25 Sep, Busan/Gyeongju): depart 06:00 → Haedong Yonggungsa Temple 07:00 → travel to Gyeongju 10:00 → Bulguksa Temple 13:00 → return Haeundae 17:00 → Airbnb 20:00. Day 3 (26 Sep, Busan→Seoul): Blue Line Park 10:00 → check out 13:00 → SEA LIFE Busan Aquarium 14:00 → KTX Busan→Seoul 19:03/21:43. Day 4 (27 Sep, Seoul): full-day Nami Island. Day 5 (28 Sep, Seoul): Bongeunsa Temple 09:00 → Lotte World Tower 11:00 → depart 15:00 → Herb Island 16:30 → return, Airbnb 23:30. Day 6 (29 Sep, Seoul): full-day Seoraksan National Park. Day 7 (30 Sep, Seoul — Saturday): depart 07:30 → Gyeongbokgung Palace 09:00 → Bukchon Hanok Village 11:30 → Changdeokgung Palace 13:30 → Gwangjang Market 16:00. Day 8 (01 Oct, Hiroshima): ICN 07:50 → FUK 08:55 → Hiroshima 11:00, rest of day free. Day 9 (02 Oct, Miyajima→Osaka): train 09:00 → ferry 10:00 → Itsukushima Shrine and Momijidani Park 10:10–21:30 → return ferry 21:30 → train 21:50 → depart Osaka 22:30, arrive 23:30. Day 10 (03 Oct, Osaka): Osaka Castle 09:00 → Umeda Sky Building 15:00 → Namco Umeda 19:00 → Royal Game Center 21:00. Day 11 (04 Oct, Osaka): Universal Studios Japan from 07:30, full day. Day 12 (05 Oct, Osaka): Universal Studios Japan 07:30 → Kaiyukan Aquarium 17:30. Day 13 (06 Oct, Osaka): Silver Ball Planet 10:00 → Dotonbori 12:30 → Nippombashi 15:30. Day 14 (07 Oct, Kyoto): Fushimi Inari Shrine 09:00 → Higashiyama district, Kiyomizu-dera and Kodai-ji 12:00 → Maruyama Park 18:00. Day 15 (08 Oct, Kyoto): Nijo Castle 11:00 → Ninja & Samurai Museum / sword experience 13:00 → Nishiki Market 15:00. Day 16 (09 Oct, Kyoto): Nanzen-ji Temple 09:00 → Saiho-ji Temple 12:00. Day 17 (10 Oct, Sapporo): NRT 08:25 → CTS → Sapporo Station 11:30 → Open Air Art Museum / Atama Daibutsu 12:10. Day 18 (11 Oct, Sapporo): onsen ryokan, free day. Day 19 (12 Oct, Tokyo): Asakusa 09:00 → Gundam Base Tokyo 11:00. Day 20 (13 Oct, Tokyo): Tokyo Character Street 09:00 → Pokémon Center Shibuya 11:00 → Akihabara 13:00 → Sensoji Temple 14:00. Day 21 (14 Oct, Tokyo): Yanaka Ginza 07:00 → Tokyo Tower 09:00 → Harajuku 11:00 → Shibuya Crossing 14:00. Day 22 (15 Oct): NRT 14:25 departure home.
known_edge_cases: 28 Sep Seoul day is the worst fatigue offender: Bongeunsa 09:00 and Lotte World Tower 11:00 are 6 metro stops apart, but Herb Island is a 2h30 / ~$45 transfer each way from Seoul, producing a 15:00 departure, a 16:30 arrival and a 23:30 return to the Airbnb — roughly 5 hours of transit stacked on the back of a full sightseeing morning.

02 Oct Miyajima day is an 11-hour island visit immediately followed by a same-night intercity move: last ferry 21:30, train 21:50, Hiroshima→Osaka 22:30 arriving 23:30, meaning the Osaka Castle 09:00 start the next morning gives under 8 hours of rest.

25 Sep Busan day chains four modes (walk 1 km → bus 1006 → Donghae line → walk 2.6 km) to reach Haedong Yonggungsa at 07:00 and then a 2h40 hop to Gyeongju; a single missed 30-minute-headway train collapses the Bulguksa 13:00 slot.
Gyeongbokgung (closed Tuesdays) and Changdeokgung (closed Mondays) were both wanted on the same day, which forces the pairing onto Wed–Sun; the trip resolved it on Saturday 30 Sep.

Blue Line Park's 4-passenger booking cap versus a party of 7 forced two separate reservations on a booking window that only opens 2 weeks ahead, and the walk from the Busan Airbnb is 41 minutes with no bus, so a taxi was the real dependency.
Ghibli Museum scored 29/35 but was dropped entirely because timed entry could not be secured a month ahead — a high-desire item silently lost to a booking constraint rather than to a scheduling one.
01 Oct requires leaving the Seoul Airbnb before dawn for a 07:50 ICN departure, immediately after the 30 Sep day that ended at Gwangjang Market at 16:00+.
Seoraksan (10h) and Nami Island (10h) are back-to-back-adjacent full-day excursions in the same city block, both consuming an entire day of the Seoul allocation of 4 days.

input_user_request: Plan a 93-day solo trip (29 Mar – 29 Jun 2025) across 16 European bases: Madrid, Lisbon, Sintra, Porto, Bordeaux, Bruges, Ghent, Edinburgh, London, Cologne, Prague, Vienna, Salzburg, Plitvice, Split and Dubrovnik. I am travelling alone on a tight budget, cooking most meals from supermarkets, and I want each city block anchored by pre-purchased timed-entry tickets so nothing is lost to sold-out days. The non-negotiable anchor of the whole trip is Sintra — I want the full palace circuit, not a day trip. Respect European closing days (many monuments close Mondays or Tuesdays), keep at most two paid museums or interiors per day so I don't burn out over three months, and make sure each city's departure day leaves enough slack for the intercity train or flight.

constraints.must_visit_location: Palácio Nacional da Pena, Sintra (the full 4-day Sintra palace circuit, 10–13 Apr 2025)
specific_hard_bounds: Museo Reina Sofía (Madrid) is closed every Tuesday; booked slot 03 Apr 2025 at 11:30 (loc. 76834084)
Templo de Debod (Madrid) opens Tue–Sun only, 10:00–20:00; visited 03 Apr at 13:30
Palacio Real (Madrid) closes at 19:00 Mon–Sat but at 16:00 on Sundays; booked 02 Apr at 12:00
Torre de Belém, Mosteiro dos Jerónimos and Panteão Nacional (Lisbon) are all Tue–Sun — a Monday in Lisbon must be routed to Alfama, Castelo or the Baixa instead
Palácio da Pena timed entry 12 Apr 2025 at 09:30 and Castelo dos Mouros 12 Apr at 14:30 — both reachable only by bus 434 from Sintra station, a single circular line
Quinta da Regaleira 11 Apr 10:00 and Palácio de Monserrat 11 Apr 12:30 are on bus 435, a different line from 434
Livraria Lello (Porto) requires a timed voucher; booked 15 Apr at 11:00 (loc. 76902679)
Taylor's Port Cellars (Porto) last admission 18:15; booked 16 Apr at 14:30
Cathédrale Saint-André (Bordeaux) opens only Wednesday and Saturday 14:30–17:30; Porte de la Grosse Cloche opens only on Saturdays
Tour Pey-Berland (Bordeaux) Tue–Sat 10:00–12:30 and 14:00–17:30 only; booked 20 Apr at 10:00 — the same day as the onward departure, requiring paid luggage storage at Bordeaux Saint-Jean
Castle of Gerald the Devil (Ghent) opens Monday only from 13:00; Sint-Baafsabdij opens Fri–Sun 14:00–18:00 only
Westminster Abbey is closed Wed 07 and Thu 08 May 2025; booked 05 May at 13:00 (order 828230)
Buckingham Palace Changing of the Guard runs only Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat at 11:00
Big Ben tour tickets are released on the second Wednesday of each month and sell out immediately
Sky Garden and Horizon 22 (London) are free but require advance timed booking
Real Mary King's Close (Edinburgh) is timed-tour only; booked 29 Apr at 17:30 (booking 41959971)
Plitvice Lakes National Park admits visitors 07:00–15:00 only; ticket booked 31 May at 09:00
Dubrovnik Old Town Walls 08:00–18:30 and explicitly must not be walked at midday due to heat and crowds
Sagrada Família (Barcelona) timed entry 27 Jun 09:45–17:15 with tickets released roughly 3 weeks out

expected_output_ground_truth: Madrid (29 Mar – 04 Apr): 31 Mar Gran Vía and Plaza de Cibeles morning → Museo del Prado 11:30. 01 Apr Puerta del Sol, Plaza de Oriente, Plaza Mayor, lunch at La Rollerie, churros San Ginés. 02 Apr Plaza de la Villa and Catedral de la Almudena morning → Palacio Real 12:00. 03 Apr Puerta de Alcalá and Retiro → Reina Sofía 11:30 with audioguide → Templo de Debod 13:30. 04 Apr Mercado de San Miguel, then airport for Lisbon. Lisbon (04–10 Apr): 05 Apr Belém axis by tram 15 — Torre de Belém, Padrão dos Descobrimentos, Jerónimos, Pilar 7, LX Factory. 06 Apr Terreiro do Paço cluster — Bacalhau centre, Lisboa Story Centre, Arco da Rua Augusta, Parque Eduardo VII. 07 Apr Sé de Lisboa, Elevador de Santa Justa, Convento do Carmo. 08 Apr Castelo de São Jorge 09:00 → Alfama → Panteão Nacional 12:30. 09 Apr Museu Nacional do Azulejo 10:00. Sintra (10–13 Apr): 11 Apr Quinta da Regaleira 10:00 → Palácio de Monserrat 12:30 (bus 435). 12 Apr Palácio da Pena 09:30 → Miradouro da Cruz Alta → Castelo dos Mouros 14:30 → Sintra Mitos e Lendas → Piriquita pastries (bus 434). 13 Apr Palácio Nacional de Sintra 09:30, then train to Porto. Porto (13–17 Apr): 14 Apr Capela das Almas, Rua Santa Catarina, Mercado do Bolhão, Torre dos Clérigos 12:30. 15 Apr São Bento, Igreja de Santo Ildefonso, Livraria Lello 11:00, Rua das Flores. 16 Apr Sé do Porto, Ribeira, Ponte Luís I, Vila Nova de Gaia → Taylor's 14:30. 17 Apr Jardins do Palácio de Cristal, then flight to Bordeaux. Bordeaux (17–21 Apr): 18 Apr Bassins des Lumières 10:00 → Cité du Vin 12:00. 19 Apr Palais Rohan, Quinconces, free walking tour, Grand Théâtre, Cathédrale Saint-André (Sat opening). 20 Apr Tour Pey-Berland 10:00 → Place de la Bourse → Porte Cailhau, luggage stored at the station, evening departure. Bruges (21–24 Apr): 22 Apr Sint-Salvator, Steenstraat, Grote Markt → Historium 14:30 → witchcraft and torture museums. 23 Apr Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk, Bonifacius Bridge, Rozenhoedkaai. 24 Apr Minnewaterpark, Fritbar lunch, laundry, train to Ghent. Ghent (24–28 Apr): 25 Apr Gerald the Devil Castle, Sint-Baafs Cathedral, Belfry. 26 Apr STAM Museum, Sint-Michielsbrug, Sint-Niklaaskerk, Sint-Baafsabdij. 27 Apr Gravensteen 10:00, Patershol, canal cruise. 28 Apr taxi to Gent-Sint-Pieters, onward to Edinburgh. Edinburgh (28 Apr – 04 May): 28 Apr Victoria Street and Bertie's. 29 Apr National Museum of Scotland → Greyfriars → Vennel → Grassmarket → Real Mary King's Close 17:30. 30 Apr Edinburgh Castle 09:30 → Princes Gardens → Ross Fountain → Tolbooth Kirk. 01 May St Giles' → Royal Mile → Holyrood Palace 12:30 → Museum of Edinburgh → Scott Monument. 02 May Calton Hill → Edinburgh Dungeon 13:00 → Stockbridge. London (04–10 May): 04 May Graffiti Tunnel. 05 May St James's Park → Changing of the Guard 11:00 → Westminster Abbey 13:00 → Big Ben exterior. 06 May St Dunstan → Sky Garden → Horizon 22 → Tower of London 13:00 → Tower Bridge. 07 May Millennium Bridge, St Paul's, Covent Garden, Neal's Yard. 08 May Trafalgar, Piccadilly, Leicester Square, Chinatown, Poppies. 09 May Outernet, Soho, Oxford Street, Mayfair Market. 10 May Natural History Museum, then flight to Cologne. Cologne (10–15 May): 11 May Heinzelmännchenbrunnen → Chocolate Museum. 12 May Heumarkt → Fragrance Museum. 13 May Kölner Dom → Alter Markt. Prague (15–21 May): 16 May Old Town Square, Municipal House, Powder Tower, Wenceslas Square, Kafka head. 19 May Prague Castle, St Vitus, Strahov, St Nicholas, Wallenstein Garden, Lennon Wall, Charles Bridge. 20 May Vyšehrad, SS Peter and Paul, Havlíčkovy sady. Vienna (21–25 May): 22 May Belvedere, Ringstraße, Stephansdom, Innere Stadt, Graben. 23 May Hofburg and Sisi Museum, Weltmuseum, Volksgarten. 24 May Schönbrunn, Rathausplatz, Staatsoper. Salzburg (25–30 May): 25 May Getreidegasse. 26 May Mirabell, Mozart's birthplace. 27 May Hohensalzburg Fortress, Hellbrunn. Plitvice (30 May – 01 Jun): 31 May park entry 09:00, full-day K route. Split (01–06 Jun): 02 Jun Diocletian's Palace, cathedral, Temple of Jupiter, underground market. 03 Jun Krka National Park day trip. Dubrovnik (06–10 Jun): 07 Jun Stradun, Pile Gate, City Walls (early morning, not midday), Orlando's Column, Sponza Palace, St Blaise; later Lokrum ferry (hourly 10:00–15:00) and Sokol Fortress.
known_edge_cases: Sintra 12 Apr chains Pena (09:30) and Castelo dos Mouros (14:30) on bus 434 with an unbudgeted Bolt ride to Pena ($12.07) and a paid car back down ($5.00) — the published bus was too slow to hold the 09:30 timed entry, so the plan silently depended on rideshare.

Sintra also mixes two non-connecting bus lines: 435 for Regaleira/Monserrat on 11 Apr and 434 for Pena/Mouros on 12 Apr, so any attempt to merge those four palaces into a single day breaks the transport model even though the opening hours would allow it.
Bordeaux 20 Apr books Tour Pey-Berland at 10:00 on the same day as departure, forcing €5.50 of station luggage storage and leaving no recovery slack if the timed entry runs late.
Cathédrale Saint-André (Wed/Sat 14:30–17:30 only) and Porte de la Grosse Cloche (Saturdays only) collapse Bordeaux's four-day block into effectively one viable Saturday for both.

Westminster Abbey's closure on 7–8 May pushed it onto 05 May, the same day as the 11:00 Changing of the Guard, so the morning had a hard 11:00 fixed event and a hard 13:00 timed entry roughly 20 minutes apart on foot.
Big Ben tours release on the second Wednesday of the month and were never secured — the item stayed on the plan as an exterior view only.
Ghent's Gerald the Devil Castle opens Mondays only from 13:00 while Sint-Baafsabdij opens Fri–Sun 14:00–18:00, so a Monday arrival day cannot host both.
Plitvice's 07:00–15:00 entry window plus a 3-day stay in the tiny village of Rastovača means a single weather-lost day has no recoverable alternate.
Dubrovnik's Old Town Walls carry an explicit 'do not do at midday' note, which is a soft comfort constraint the schedule must honour even though the venue is open 08:00–18:30.

As a solo traveller cooking from supermarkets, the plan repeatedly places a supermarket run on arrival evenings (Lisbon 05 Apr, Sintra 10 Apr, Porto 13 Apr, Bordeaux 17 Apr, Bruges 21 Apr, Ghent 24 Apr) — an unstated recurring block a naive planner would fill with sightseeing.

The 93-day duration makes cumulative fatigue the dominant risk: Madrid alone stacks Prado (31 Mar), Palacio Real (02 Apr) and Reina Sofía + Debod (03 Apr) in five days, and only the one-museum-per-day pacing kept it viable.

input_user_request: Plan a 26-day trip (19 Sep – 14 Oct 2019) for a group of 6 travellers who voted on candidate cities, covering Venice, Athens, the Cyclades island chain, Budapest, Kraków, Rome, Zagreb/Plitvice and Paris. The group's top-voted destination is Venice (22/25) and the strongest single-country pull is Greece, so the Cyclades island-hopping segment is the spine of the trip: Santorini, Milos, Naxos and Mykonos in four consecutive days, each connected by a morning ferry. Ferries are the binding constraint — most tickets must be collected in person at a local travel agency before boarding, and there is exactly one sailing per day on several of these legs. Budget is shared and low, so several intercity moves are overnight buses to save a night of lodging.

constraints.must_visit_location: Cyclades island chain — Santorini → Milos → Naxos → Mykonos, four consecutive one-night stays (25–29 Sep 2019)
specific_hard_bounds: Overnight ferry Piraeus (Athens) → Thira (Santorini) departs strictly 20:30 on 24 Sep and arrives 05:30 on 25 Sep; physical tickets must be collected at the Piraeus port office before boarding
Ferry Santorini → Milos departs strictly 08:30 on 26 Sep, arrives 10:35; tickets must be collected in person at Nomikos Travel & Tourist Office in Santorini the day before
Ferry Milos → Naxos departs strictly 08:10 on 27 Sep, arrives 10:30; tickets collected in person at Riva Travel, Milos
Ferry Naxos → Mykonos departs strictly 09:35 on 28 Sep, arrives 11:05; tickets collected in person at Passenger Tours, Naxos
Flight Mykonos (JMK) → Budapest (BUD) departs 06:40 on 29 Sep — the airport transfer must start around 04:30, immediately after a single night on the island
Overnight bus Budapest Népliget → Kraków MDA departs 23:30 on 01 Oct, arrives 06:50 on 02 Oct
Auschwitz-Birkenau + Wieliczka Salt Mines combined guided tour is a single fixed full-day slot: 04 Oct 2019 at 09:00 (voucher GYG32QLWLKM7)
Overnight bus Rome Tiburtina → Zagreb departs 21:20 on 08 Oct and arrives 09:55 on 09 Oct — 12h35 in transit
Plitvice day trip is locked to the bus timetable: Zagreb 05:45 → Plitvice 08:10, park ticket 09:00, return bus 17:50 → Zagreb 20:20
Flight Zagreb (ZAG) → Paris (CDG) departs 17:55 on 11 Oct
Airport bus Venice Marco Polo → Piazzale Roma is pre-booked for specific departures (20:00 arrival leg, 19:10 departure leg) and the flight to Athens leaves VCE at 21:55 on 22 Sep, landing 01:15
Venice accommodation is 2 nights only and the group's own vote gave Venice the highest score, so its two days cannot be reduced

expected_output_ground_truth: 20 Sep: land Venice Marco Polo, pre-booked bus 20:00 → Piazzale Roma 20:20, check in near Calle del Magazzen. 21 Sep (Venice, full day): Piazza San Marco with Basilica and Palazzo Ducale, Rialto Bridge, Grand Canal, Santa Maria della Salute, Bridge of Sighs, Jewish Ghetto, Frari, Giardini Papadopoli. 22 Sep (Venice → Athens): morning in Venice, bus 19:10 → Marco Polo 19:30, flight 21:55, land Athens 01:15 on 23 Sep. 23 Sep (Athens): Acropolis and Parthenon, Plaka, Monastiraki, Ancient Agora. 24 Sep (Athens → ferry): Temple of Olympian Zeus, Roman Agora, Central Market, Filopappou Hill; collect ferry tickets at Piraeus, board 20:30 overnight sailing. 25 Sep (Santorini): dock Thira 05:30, day in Santorini and Kamari, collect next-day ferry tickets at Nomikos Travel. 26 Sep (Milos): ferry 08:30 → Milos 10:35, Sarakiniko and Adamantas, collect tickets at Riva Travel. 27 Sep (Naxos): ferry 08:10 → Naxos 10:30, Naxos town and beaches, collect tickets at Passenger Tours. 28 Sep (Mykonos): ferry 09:35 → Mykonos 11:05, Chora and Agrari, early night before the dawn flight. 29 Sep (Budapest): flight 06:40 → BUD 09:15, Parliament and Shoes on the Danube, Chain Bridge. 30 Sep – 01 Oct (Budapest): Fisherman's Bastion and Matthias Church, Gellért Baths, Váci utca; overnight bus 23:30 to Kraków. 02 Oct (Kraków): arrive 06:50, Main Market Square, Florian Gate. 03 Oct (Kraków): Kazimierz Jewish Quarter, former ghetto, Schindler's Factory. 04 Oct (Kraków): full-day Auschwitz-Birkenau + Wieliczka combined tour from 09:00. 05 Oct (Kraków → Rome): flight KRK 19:05 → Ciampino 21:05. 06–08 Oct (Rome): three days of the historic centre; 08 Oct evening board the 21:20 overnight bus to Zagreb. 09 Oct (Zagreb): arrive 09:55, recover, Radićeva street and upper town. 10 Oct (Plitvice): bus 05:45 → Plitvice 08:10 → park entry 09:00 → full K route → return bus 17:50 → Zagreb 20:20. 11 Oct (Zagreb → Paris): morning free, flight 17:55 → CDG 20:00. 12–13 Oct (Paris): Eiffel Tower, Place de la Concorde, Saint-Jacques Tower and Sainte-Chapelle, Catacombs. 14 Oct: return home.
known_edge_cases: Every Cyclades leg is a single daily sailing with a hard departure between 08:10 and 09:35, and each ticket had to be collected in person at a different named agency on the previous island — so a missed collection, not a missed boat, is the real failure mode, and there is no same-day recovery sailing.

Four islands in four nights means each island effectively yields one afternoon: dock 10:30–11:05, sightsee, sleep, re-board the next morning. Any planner that treats these as 'one day per island' overstates available time by roughly half.

28–29 Sep is the sharpest fatigue break: arrive Mykonos 11:05 after a 09:35 ferry, single night, then a 06:40 flight requiring a ~04:30 departure to JMK — under 6 hours of sleep bracketed by two transport events.

Two overnight buses (Budapest→Kraków 23:30–06:50 and Rome→Zagreb 21:20–09:55) save lodging but delete the following morning: the Kraków arrival at 06:50 precedes check-in, and the 09:55 Zagreb arrival is followed the next day by a 05:45 bus to Plitvice.

Plitvice is a fixed round trip with no flexibility on either end: the 05:45 outbound and 17:50 return are the only usable services, so the 09:00 park entry and the entire day's route are dictated by the bus timetable rather than by the park.

The 04 Oct Auschwitz + Wieliczka combined tour is a single 09:00 full-day commitment covering two emotionally and physically heavy sites — it consumes the day entirely and should never be paired with additional museums.
The Venice departure on 22 Sep has the pre-booked 19:10 airport bus, a 21:55 flight and a 01:15 Athens landing, meaning the 23 Sep Acropolis day starts on roughly four hours of sleep.

Group size shifted mid-planning (one traveller left and another joined for the Zagreb, Plitvice and Paris legs), so several bookings carry a '-Dorjaen +Veronica' note — headcount is not constant across the itinerary and per-person costs change after 09 Oct.
